newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Moslems say Ethiopia attacks their Somalia base.
newsitem.headline: Moslems say Ethiopia attacks their Somalia base.

text.p: A Moslem fundamentalist group, al-Ittihad al-Islam, said that Ethiopian troops had attacked one of its bases in western Somalia on Sunday and killed several Islamic guerrillas.

There was no independent confirmation of the report, but it came from an area where an Ethiopian force last month crossed into Somalia with the aim of eliminating what Ethiopia called "terrorist" bases.

Ahmed Bile, secretary of the al-Ittihad al-Islam group, told reporters in Mogadishu that the Ethiopians crossed into Somalia in Dolaw district of Gedo region, 500 km (300 miles) southwest of Mogadishu.
Reports from the area indicated that the attack was continuing and the al-Ittihad fighters were resisting, he said.

Ethiopia mounted a strong armed attack into Somalia last month against the Moslem fundamentalists, whom Ethiopia blamed for recent bomb attacks in Addis Ababa. It said the attacks were directed against the fundamentalists' bases and training camps.

During last month's attack, the Ethiopians seized control of three Somali towns before withdrawing. Ethiopian officials later said their forces might return for more attacks against what they called a "multinational terrorist group" operating from Somalia.
Al-Ittihad said that its forces killed at least 150 Ethiopian soldiers while resisting last month's attack. The group said it also downed an Ethiopian helicopter and destroyed a tank.
Little is known of the shadowy fundamentalist group and its role in Somalia. But Islamic sources in Mogadishu said on Sunday that it was being funded from the Middle East.

A Somali faction leader, Omar Haji Mohamed, a former general in the Somali army before president Mohamed Siad Barre was ousted in 1991, has denied claims by al-Ittihad that his supporters fought alongside the Ethiopians in the August attacks.
But there were reports in Mogadishu that the fundamentalist group, whose members come from several Arab countries, were supported by Somali fundamentalists.
